### Problem

On 2026-11-08 the maintainer had to add, remove or re-add a label by hand six times to move issues and pull requests the flow should have moved by itself. Each time had a cause in the engine: G1 passed #698 while the autopilot's start check refused it (the `dx-release-lane` marker, which `scripts/issue-schema.py` MARKER does not know); an issue fixed by an edit does not start the autopilot, only a label does; a failed conventions check on an autopilot pull request (#689, the title's type against its files) waits on "the autopilot" for 14 hours with nothing running; a hint on a pull request without `needs-human` is ignored; a maintainer's decision outside the code (a sub-issue, #695) does not re-run the review, so its finding stays open; and a bug the release lane opens, with the run that shows it, is triaged `could-not-reproduce` and waits on `accepted` instead of going the reproduced way.

### Scope

- One check of an issue's shape, the same code for G1 and for the autopilot's start, which knows every marker the engine writes.
- An accepted issue whose text becomes valid starts the autopilot, as an acceptance does.
- The autopilot fixes a failed conventions check on its own pull request (the title's type, a commit's header), as it fixes any failed check.
- A hint of someone who decides, on an autopilot pull request that waits on the autopilot, brings it back, stopped or not.
- An answer of someone who decides that settles a review finding outside the code re-runs the review.
- A bug the release lane opens is accepted by policy as reproduced: its run is the reproduction.

### Out of scope

The paths and the stop of #696's C1 and C2, worked there.

### Acceptance criteria

C1: Given an issue with any marker the engine writes before its first section, when G1 and the autopilot's start check it, then both give the same answer, from the same function.
C2: Given an accepted issue the autopilot refused for its shape, when its text is edited and passes, then the autopilot starts without a label.
C3: Given an autopilot pull request whose conventions check failed, when the check ends, then the autopilot's fix round runs on it and corrects the title or commits.
C4: Given an autopilot pull request that waits on the autopilot, when someone who decides comments a hint, then the autopilot runs with it.
C5: Given a review finding that someone who decides settles in a comment, when they answer, then the review runs again on the same head.
C6: Given the release lane opens a bug, when it is opened, then it is accepted by policy as a reproduced bug and the autopilot starts on it.
C7: Given each of C1 to C6, when the release lane plays its scenarios, then a scenario plays it and passes, with no person adding or removing a label.

### Criticality

Critical
